description: #152 found that a kilogram of sulphuryl difluoride from a rural stack was worth 4,630 kg CO2-eq and the same kilogram over a suburb was worth nothing, and answered it with a rule that carried one air factor across every air sub-compartment in three well-mixed categories, indoor and long-term air included. That rule is retired: `data/context-carry-rules.json` carries the outdoor strata from unspecified air in every category, and indoor and long-term air are walls nothing crosses. This file replaces `0731-one-air-factor-covers-every-compartment.json`, whose indoor expectations it deliberately inverts.

expectations.title: Sulphuryl difluoride released over a suburb is worth what it is worth from a stack

subject.context_display: Environmental → Air → Ground level → Urban (>1000 people/square mile)

expectations.comment: The expectation the first rule was written for, kept. The urban ground level takes unspecified air's number under the convention, and unspecified air carries the 4,630 a ruling published (#151).

expectations.title: The same kilogram released indoors is not characterised
expectations.comment: Indoor air is a wall of the convention: a different fate model, and one convention has no per-category holes in a wall. The first rule carried fifteen indoor factors for HFCs and halons on the strength of the gas being well mixed; they are withdrawn with it, and whether a greenhouse gas should cross this wall is recorded as an open decision in `plans/lcia-consensus-decisions.md` §9 rather than answered by a category list.

expectations.title: A high urban stack takes the rural stack's number
expectations.comment: The downward rules carry 1,515 factors for EF 3.1 on the 2026-09-01 build -- 1,029 rivers, 121 lakes, 170 silvicultural and 125 industrial soils, 30 non-agricultural soils, and 40 air strata -- and 8,257 for Stepwise. Bounded from below rather than pinned, because the count grows with every list that brings a context somebody else characterised; what must not happen is the pass going silent, which a thousand guards against.
